title: NASA Is Hiring Astronauts — Could You Be Next?
summary:
NASA wants new astronauts. Could one of them be you — one day?

NASA is looking for its next generation of astronauts to help carry out future missions to the Moon and, eventually, Mars. Landing a seat on the rocket, however, will take far more than a dream of spaceflight.

To be eligible, applicants must be US citizens with a master's degree in a STEM field: science, technology, engineering, or mathematics. NASA will also accept a select few other qualifications instead. All candidates need at least three years of relevant professional experience, and they must pass a physical exam to show they can handle the demands of spaceflight. Applications close December 3, 2026.

NASA will then carefully review each application. A small number of candidates will be invited for interviews, and an even smaller number will be selected. The odds are steep: during the last selection process in 2024, the space agency chose just 10 people from more than 8,000 applicants. This year's new astronaut class will be announced in late 2027.

The chosen hopefuls will begin two years of intensive training in early 2028. They will take part in simulated spacewalks, learn to operate spacecraft, and control robotic arms. They will also develop survival skills on land and in water.

The new recruits will join NASA at an exciting time. Through its ongoing Artemis program, NASA plans to send astronauts to explore the Moon's South Pole. Eventually, they will build a base where people can live, work, and conduct research. The new astronauts could help make these plans a reality and prepare for future missions to Mars.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman says the people selected could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems that will ultimately carry crews to Mars.
why_it_matters: NASA's choice will shape who explores the Moon and prepares the way to Mars, and it shows young people what study and training it takes to reach space.

background_read: NASA is the United States space agency, and its astronauts are the people who fly into space and carry out missions there.
Every few years NASA opens applications for a new group of astronauts, choosing only a small number from thousands of hopefuls.
Once chosen, new astronauts spend years training for spacewalks, flying spacecraft, and working with robotic arms before they ever leave Earth.
The new group will support the Artemis program, which aims to send astronauts to explore the Moon's South Pole and, one day, on to Mars.
